William Butler Yeats was an Irish poet and playwright, born in Dublin in 1865, and the leading figure of the Irish literary revival. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923.

He drew on Irish myth and folklore, and with Lady Gregory founded the Abbey Theatre in Dublin in 1904 as a national theatre. His early poems are dreamy and romantic; his later ones, such as Easter, 1916 and The Second Coming, are among the most quoted poems in English.

He wrote about the Easter Rising and served as a senator of the Irish Free State. He was part of the Gaelic revival that also produced the GAA. He was the first Irish winner of the Nobel Prize, and with Joyce he made Ireland a power in modern literature.
sum: William Butler Yeats was an Irish poet and playwright, born in Dublin in 1865, and the leading figure of the Irish literary revival. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923.
